article: Acoustic levitation: standing waves, radiation force and ultrasonic physics
findings: The article incorrectly inferred zero net force from zero cycle-mean first-order pressure and stated a universal sound-level threshold for second-order effects.
The 1D standing-wave force coefficient was corrected from 5/6 to 5/2 under the explicitly stated peak-pressure and f1=f2=1 assumptions.
The equilibrium equation includes air buoyancy through effective weight (rho_p-rho_0)V_p g, with the rho_p >> rho_0 approximation identified.
Gor’kov’s Rayleigh small-sphere condition is a model applicability assumption, not a universal maximum levitatable size; large-drop and atomization results depend on experimental conditions.
Unsupported universal phased-array capabilities, droplet breakup thresholds, sound-level limits, and no-harm/no-contamination implications were removed or qualified.
The review compares the complete Japanese article with all twelve translations, including formulas, diagrams where present, terminology, bibliography and claims.

meaning.note: Compared the complete article against Japanese: first-order pressure versus mean force, standing-wave node/antinode geometry, Gor’kov assumptions and force derivation, phased-array evidence, size limits, sound-level qualifications, droplet deformation, applications and conclusion.

terminology.note: Checked localized terminology for acoustic radiation force/pressure, pressure and velocity nodes, Rayleigh regime, Gor’kov potential, phased arrays, droplet breakup and sound-pressure levels; unsupported absolute wording was replaced with condition-specific wording.

mathematics.note: Re-derived the 1D standing-wave potential and vertical force under the stated peak-pressure and f1=f2=1 assumptions; corrected coefficient to 5/2, checked RMS caveat, buoyancy-adjusted weight, coordinate direction and limits of a 1D stability claim.

code.note: Checked the translated Mermaid diagram and its claims; there is no runnable program code.

links.note: Checked the bibliography links and matching destinations for Gor’kov (1962), Marzo et al. (2015), Cancino-Jaque et al. (2023), and Saroj & Thaokar (2024).

post/acoustic-levitation-standing-waves-.summary: Reviewed the complete translation against the Japanese source, corrected unsupported claims about acoustic forces, phased-array manipulation and universal limits, clarified model assumptions and equilibrium interpretation, and checked cited sources.
limitations: AI review only; no human or native-speaker certification.
Cited experiments and models were checked against the named publications but were not independently replicated.
The Gor’kov derivation is limited to its stated small-sphere/ideal-fluid assumptions; practical stability and operating limits require system-specific measurement.
